skill.name: task-runner
skill.description: Run and inspect project tasks through the just command runner. It helps users discover recipes, run tests, build projects, lint code, and invoke project-specific commands.
skill.summary: Discover and run project just recipes for tests, builds, linting, and other common development tasks.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: The static findings are Markdown command examples and code fences, not Ruby backtick execution in executable code. A semantic review found one real workflow risk: the skill encourages running repository-defined just recipes through Bash, which can execute arbitrary project commands if the repository is untrusted.

remediation.suggestion: Inspect the justfile and recipe body before running commands from an untrusted project.

remediation.issue: High-impact recipes such as deploy or clean
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running deployment, cleanup, or argument-bearing recipes.
Add instructions to prefer just --list and just --show before executing unfamiliar recipes.

semantic_findings.title: Repository-Defined Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the agent to execute project-specific just recipes through Bash. Recipes in an untrusted justfile can run arbitrary shell commands, including deployment or cleanup actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The purpose and examples explicitly direct execution of repository-defined recipes. The risk depends on project trust and user confirmation, so confidence is high for the behavior but not for malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Project commands are often hidden across scripts, docs, and package files. This skill discovers just recipes and runs common tasks from one workflow.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether a project uses a justfile for task automation.
Lists available just recipes before running project commands.
Runs common recipes such as test, build, lint, and dev.
Shows recipe details with just discovery commands.
Supports project-specific recipes with arguments when requested.
limitations: Requires the just CLI to be installed on the user system.
Only works when the project provides a justfile or compatible recipe file.
Recipe behavior depends on project-maintained commands and scripts.
High-impact tasks should be reviewed before execution.

best_practices: Run discovery commands before executing unfamiliar recipes.
Inspect deployment, cleanup, and argument-based recipes before use.
Keep common project workflows documented in the justfile.
anti_patterns: Running recipes from untrusted repositories without inspection.
Using deployment recipes without confirming the target environment.
Assuming recipe names are safe without checking their command bodies.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps discover and run project tasks defined in a justfile.

faq.question: Does it require just?
faq.answer: Yes. The just command line tool must be installed before recipes can run.

faq.question: Can it run tests and builds?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed for common recipes such as test, build, lint, and dev.

faq.question: Can it run commands in subdirectories?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use a specific justfile path when the project stores recipes in a subdirectory.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted projects?
faq.answer: Use caution. Review the justfile before running recipes from an untrusted repository.

faq.question: Does it create a justfile?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on discovering and running recipes that already exist.
